absent: Full field layout and lifetime rules for execution parameter, binary format, memory, file, credential, namespace, and filesystem objects beyond observed field uses.
Contracts and failure modes for binary loader callbacks, interpreter files, descriptor passing handover, and loader substitutes.
Security, audit, scheduler, accounting, restart handling, user event, and connector interactions surrounding execution.
Stack area creation, argument page acquisition, mapping, cache maintenance, and memory reclaim behavior.
Compatibility user pointer translation, user string length measurement, and user memory fault handling details.
Polling item, wait entry, and head object layouts, watch enforcement, and tunable initialization beyond boot setup.
System control registration mechanics and dump safety revalidation triggered by dumpability changes.
Signal pending detection, scheduling cooperation, resource limit accounting, and restart versus failure code selection.
File open, close, read, and reference counting behavior for executables, interpreters, and descriptor derived paths.
Thread group traversal, filesystem sharing counts, and sequence protection guarantees during unsafe assessment.

findings.text: Provides registration for executable format handlers with caller choice of front versus back placement on the shared format list. Relies on exclusive protection during list mutation.
Exposes a query for the close on exec marking of a descriptor number for the calling process file table, evaluated as a bit test against the current descriptor table snapshot.
Supplies a caller owned reference to the failure filesystem root location by copying the stored path and elevating its reference count.
Allows kernel initiated execution from kernel resident argument and environment vectors, rejecting invocation from kernel threads and rejecting empty argument vectors.

Boot time setup for the event polling subsystem that establishes a per user watch allowance derived from available low memory and creates dedicated slab caches for core polling objects before enabling related tunables.

User facing execution entries for native and compatibility argument layouts, with and without explicit directory file descriptor and flags, all converging on a shared common execution path after filename resolution.
Boot registration of filesystem execution tunables under the filesystem control hierarchy.

Argument vector view that abstracts native versus compatibility user pointer arrays behind a discriminator and a union holding one of the two user array pointer flavors, with indexed fetch translating compatibility entries to native user pointers and reporting access faults through error pointers.

The format list is guarded by a read write lock held exclusively for registration and shared for handler search, with the shared hold temporarily released while invoking a candidate loader and reacquired before releasing the candidate reference and deciding whether to continue.

Credential preparation acquires the signal credential guard interruptibly and retains it across execution setup; failure cleanup clears the in execution mark, releases the guard, and abandons the staged credentials, while the filesystem in execution mark is set while this guard is held.

Short critical sections protect stack limit sampling with the group leader task lock, filesystem sharing assessment with exclusive sequence protection, and file table flag and thread and pid observations with read side protection.

The per user watch ceiling stored for later enforcement equals low memory quantity divided by twenty five scaled by page size then normalized by per item cost, is required to be non negative, and coexists with a build time requirement that the polling item stay within a small size bound on narrow pointer systems.

Polling relies on three dedicated slab caches for item, wait entry, and batched head objects, all requiring panic on allocation failure and accounting, with the item cache additionally requiring hardware cache alignment.

Dumpability for privileged transitions defaults to disabled and is exposed through a writable control that only accepts a small bounded range; a successful write that changes the value triggers a dump safety revalidation.

User and kernel string vector lengths are bounded by a maximum string count, cooperate with scheduling, abort on pending fatal signals, and map null termination, access faults, and over limit counts to distinct outcomes.

The argument and environment stack allowance is the smaller of a fixed stack fraction and a quarter of the current stack resource limit but never below a historic minimum, reduced by space needed for argument and environment pointer tables with overflow and plausibility checks, and rejected when the current stack position already lies below the computed floor.

String contents are staged in reverse order toward lower stack positions with per string length validation, stack floor enforcement, signal cooperation, and reuse of a single mapped page while consecutive bytes remain within the same page.

Argument page slots release idempotently: populated slots are freed and cleared to null while empty slots are left untouched, and one configuration defines the bulk release as a no operation while the other releases every slot in the table.

Execution parameter blocks own a fresh address space, user namespace reference, argument pages, staged credentials, and opened files; cleanup releases each owned resource exactly once, clears execution marks, handles unconsumed loader and interpreter substitutes, and tolerates partially initialized blocks.

The executed name uses the supplied path directly for current directory or absolute lookups and otherwise synthesizes a descriptor based path, marks descriptor derived names that will become inaccessible due to close on exec, and records whether the operation is an access check rather than a real transition.

Execution is marked unsafe for privilege sensitive decisions when under ptrace, when no new privileges mode is active, or when the filesystem context is shared beyond the current thread group; otherwise the filesystem is marked as in execution to block sharing clones until threading is resolved.

Handler selection starts by zeroing a fixed size header buffer and reading the file prefix from the beginning, applying a security precheck, then trialing registered handlers until one succeeds or signals an irreversible commitment, with unknown formats reported distinctly from loader failures.

Execution setup allocates a new memory descriptor, captures a user namespace reference and a snapshot of the stack resource limit, and establishes an initial stack mapping with failure unwinding that drops the descriptor without leaking the partially built state.
Close on exec state is determined by testing the descriptor bit in the current file table descriptor bitmap.
The failure filesystem root path object begins zero initialized and is handed out by value copy with its reference elevated for the caller.

Execution occupies counting, staging, credential, loading, and completion states. Counting and staging failures remain before credential commitment and unwind the parameter block. Credential and loading failures after irreversible commitment force process termination rather than returning to user code. Successful loading advances to scheduler, accounting, and notification completion.

Loader resolution allows a bounded number of interpreter substitutions. Each iteration that yields an interpreter swaps the active file while discarding loader specific substitutes, preserves an executable handle only for descriptor passing mode, and otherwise closes the replaced file. Exceeding the bound reports a loop condition, and completion without a pending interpreter proceeds to auditing and event reporting.

Format trialing holds shared protection while selecting candidates, drops protection while invoking the candidate with an elevated module reference, then reestablishes protection to release the reference. Trials continue only for unrecognized format reports without irreversible commitment; any other outcome or commitment terminates the search.

User memory access faults, oversized vectors or strings, stack exhaustion, interrupted credential guard acquisition, and pending fatal signals are mapped to distinct failure codes that abort execution before commitment, while failures after the point of no return are converted into fatal process termination when no fatal signal is already pending.

Boot time misconfiguration of watch accounting and oversized polling structures are treated as fatal build or boot errors, exec initiation from kernel threads and empty kernel argument vectors are rejected as invalid, and launching with a null argument vector emits a one time warning while repairing the vector with an empty string.
The dumpability control appears under the filesystem hierarchy with read write owner and read group and other permissions and accepts only values from zero through two inclusive.

Named bounds govern maximum argument strings, maximum single string length, maximum argument pages, historic argument byte allowance, stack fraction denominator, and binary header prefix size used for format detection.

Named indicators distinguish current directory lookup, descriptor based execution checks, descriptor derived path inaccessibility, ptrace and privilege and sharing unsafe reasons, execution file descriptor retention, and execution event reporting.
